category: usenet provider (volume plans with a 14-day trial)

free_tier.stated: A free 14-day trial on every package; a third-party index states it carries 10 GB of high-speed data.
free_tier.notes: The 10 GB allowance is from usenet.org, not the vendor page.

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap is published; retrieval is by Usenet article over NNTP
per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: unverified: the packages page read does not state retention

egress.terms: Metered by plan: 35, 70 or 140 GB of high-speed data a month, plus a 600 GB flat-rate volume at 2 Mbit/s
egress.free_allowance: 35 GB high-speed volume per month on the smallest plan

interface_detail: NNTP with 256-bit SSL; the vendor ships a free newsreader
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: Four plans: a monthly Starter at EUR 13.99 and one-time Flex, Expert and Master volumes; every plan adds a 600 GB flat-rate volume at 2 Mbit/s that keeps a slow background download running after the high-speed volume is used.

limits.value: 35 GB high-speed volume on Starter and Flex, 70 GB on Expert, 140 GB on Master
600 GB a month flat-rate volume at a maximum of 2 Mbit/s

limits_note: Starter EUR 13.99 monthly debit, Flex EUR 8.33 one-time, Expert EUR 9.83 one-time, Master EUR 14.99 one-time.
binding_note: The high-speed volume is a fixed number of GB, after which the 2 Mbit/s flat volume applies.

identity_cost.detail: The FAQ states a minimum age of 18 to sign up and lists PayPal, Credit Card and, in six named countries, Direct Debit as payment methods; the registration form itself was not opened, so its other fields are unverified.

reliability_note: Backbone and retention are not stated on the vendor page read.
confidence_note: Plan prices and the trial are from the vendor packages page read on 2026-11-03; the 10 GB allowance is third-party.
